correctness.rationale: For any periodic orbit, count directed contacts and use disjointness of excitation times separated by two to obtain equality in the local half-degree budget. Every neighbor of an active vertex is then active; connectedness forces global activity, and each vertex-triangle locks a local excitation to exactly 3-step recurrence. The coloring equivalence and Johnson 4-clique/exception argument complete the proof. Independent finite all-state and phase-coloring scripts passed from their actual paths. Infinite conclusions rest on proof, not sampling.

value.rationale: A structural mechanism excludes all long waves at a sharp contact threshold on a broad nonregular graph class; it yields a complete all-k Johnson family dichotomy, with a single exceptional octahedral graph, and explains persistence on triangle-free graphs. This adds a genuine all-recurrent-period result beyond previously known immediate three-cycle statements and strict-density extinction criteria.
